name: Rh Isoimmunization, Fetal Anemia and Intrauterine Transfusion

reference.source: Sakshi Arora Obstetrics 9th Edition / RCOG Green-top Guideline on Alloimmunization
clinicalPearls: Fetomaternal hemorrhage in RhD-negative mothers elicits maternal anti-D IgG antibodies that cross placenta and hemolyze fetal RBCs
Critical maternal indirect Coombs test titer threshold is typically 1:16 to 1:32 warranting fetal surveillance
Middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity (MCA PSV) Doppler exceeding 1.5 multiples of the median predicts moderate-to-severe fetal anemia
Intrauterine transfusion via umbilical vein cordocentesis using O-negative CMV-negative irradiated packed red cells is definitive therapy
Routine anti-D prophylaxis requires 300 mcg IM at 28 weeks and within 72 hours postpartum, plus extra doses for sensitizing events
reference.pathophysiology: Rh isoimmunization develops when an RhD-negative woman carries an RhD-positive fetus. Transplacental passage of fetal red cells exposes the maternal immune system to the foreign D surface antigen. An initial IgM response shifts to high-affinity anti-D IgG antibodies. In subsequent Rh-positive pregnancies, IgG antibodies freely cross the syncytiotrophoblast, coating fetal erythrocytes and precipitating splenic extravascular destruction. Severe anemia causes hepatic hematopoiesis, portal hypertension, hypoalbuminemia, and hydrops fetalis.
additionalDifferentials: Non-immune hydrops fetalis (parvovirus B19, alpha-thalassemia major, Turner syndrome)
ABO incompatibility (milder, rarely causes hydrops in utero)
Other red cell alloantibodies (anti-Kell, anti-c, anti-E)
additionalInvestigations: Maternal blood group and indirect Coombs test (ICT) antibody titration
Serial fetal middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity (MCA PSV) Doppler ultrasound
Kleihauer-Betke acid elution test on maternal blood to quantify fetomaternal hemorrhage
Percutaneous umbilical blood sampling (cordocentesis) for fetal hematocrit
